# What
## does
### this
#### do? 

plain text

*Italicized text*

**bold text**

***bold and italic***

- First item
- Second item

1. First step
2. Second step

`mean()` is an R function

- warning = FALSE -> do not show warning messages in the final output
- error = FALSE -> if there's an error, stop the knit / error = TRUE -> if there's an error, keep knitting and show the error message in the final output
- message = FALSE -> do not show informational messages, such as package start up messages, in the final output
- echo = FALSE -> hide the code, but still shows the results
- echo = TRUE -> show the code and the results
- include = FALSE -> execute the code, but do not show the code and the results in the final doc

#### Required packages
```{r required packages, warning = FALSE, error = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(gtsummary)
library(vtable)
library(readxl)
library(reportRmd)
library(infer)
library(rstatix)
```

```{r load the data}
test <- read_csv("test.csv")
head(test, 10)
glimpse(test)
vtable(test)
```

```{r create categorical variable for age}
test <- test %>% mutate(age_cat = case_when(
  is.na(age) ~ NA_character_,
  age < 45 ~ "<45",
  age >= 45 & age < 50 ~ "45-49",
  age >= 50 & age < 55 ~ "50-54",
  age >= 55 & age < 60 ~ "55-59",
  age >= 60 & age < 65 ~ "60-64",
  TRUE ~ "65+"
))

table(test$age, test$age_cat)
```

```{r recoding ethnicity variable}
test <- test %>% mutate(ethnicity = case_when(
  ethgrp == 1 ~ "Black",
  ethgrp == 2 ~ "White",
  ethgrp == 3 ~ "Other"
))

table(test$ethgrp, test$ethnicity)
```

```{r chi-square test}
test$stroke_factor <- as.factor(test$stroke)

table(test$gender, test$stroke)
table(test$gender, test$stroke_factor)

infer::chisq_test(test, gender ~ stroke_factor) # from infer package
chisq.test(test$gender, test$stroke) # base R version
```
```{r fishers test}
xtab <- table(test$gender, test$stroke)
fisher_test(xtab, detailed = TRUE) # tidyverse version

fisher.test(test$gender, test$stroke) # base R version
```

```{r shapiro wilk test}
test_data_female <- filter(test, gender == "f")
shapiro.test(test_data_female$age)
```

```{r t-test}
t.test(age ~ gender, data = test, var.equal = FALSE)
var.test(age ~ gender, data = test)
t.test(age ~ gender, data = test, var.equal = TRUE)
```

```{r correlation}
cor.test(test$ldl1, test$ldl2, method = "spearman")
cor.test(test$ldl1, test$ldl2, method = "pearson")
```

## Linear regression

```{r linear regression}
linear_model <- lm(age ~ as.factor(gender) + ldl1, data = test)
summary(linear_model)
gtsummary::tbl_regression(linear_model)
```

```{r logistic regression}
logistic_model <- glm(Cancer ~ as.factor(gender) + ldl1 + smoking, data = test, family = "binomial")
summary(logistic_model)
gtsummary::tbl_regression(logistic_model)
exp(cbind(OR = coef(logistic_model), confint(logistic_model)))
gtsummary::tbl_regression(logistic_model, exponentiate = TRUE)
```

```{r one way ANOVA}
one_anova <- aov(age ~ ethgrp, data = test)
summary(one_anova)
```

```{r non-parametric ANOVA}
kruskal.test(age ~ ethgrp, data = test)
```

#### Exercise 1
Using the test dataset:

1. Add a heading called "Age Distribution"
2. Insert an R code chunk and create a histogram of age using ggplot
3. Add labels (title, x-axis, and y-axis)
4. Add one sentence description of the histogram
5. Knit and check if the plot and the code are visible. 

## Age Distribution

```{r age distribution histogram}
age_distribution <- ggplot(test, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, color = "white", fill = "blue") +
  labs(
    title = "Age Distribution",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Count"
  )

age_distribution
```
